caption:
What a Pushword carousel can render, one feature per slide: the text stack, anchors and alignment, per-slide palettes, highlighted titles, free text boxes, focal-point crops, split frames and deck-wide background effects.

The whole deck is a small JSON file. Validate it, then export the images from the studio.

slides.title: Three fields, one stack
slides.paragraph: A tagline, uppercased in the accent colour. A title, in the heading font. A paragraph, in the body one. Each is optional, and a \n breaks a line where you want it.

slides.title:
Anchored top,
set right
slides.paragraph: layout anchors the stack top, center or bottom; align sets left, center or right. textScale nudges the whole stack — this one sits at 0.9.

slides.title:
Your own palette,
per slide
slides.paragraph: This slide overrides the deck palette and switches the background effect off. highlight paints a rounded marker behind each title line.

texts.content: Every coordinate is a fraction of the frame, so a box lands in the same place at any format.
Small print, at size 0.02: a photo credit, a source, a disclaimer.

slides.title: A focal point, not a crop
slides.paragraph: focusX, focusY and zoom keep the subject in frame — a landscape photo fills this portrait slide, and the same three numbers still work at any other format.

slides.title:
Two images,
one frame
slides.paragraph: split-v gives each photo half the height, and its own focal point.

slides.title: The same pair, turned
slides.paragraph: split-h stands them side by side. Text stays bound to the deck margins, so it reads across either split.

slides.title:
Thirteen effects,
one canvas
slides.paragraph: An effect is drawn once across the whole deck and sliced per slide, so a shape cut by one swipe resumes on the next.

slides.title: Edit it, then delete it
slides.paragraph: Open this deck in the studio, move a slide, export the images. Then remove it from Social posts in the admin — it is the only carousel here.
